page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The configuration includes 4 virtual CPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, and a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

The instance includes 150 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AES cryptography. No GPU hardware is present on this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the r5dn.xlarge exhibits weak single-core and multi-core CPU performance, falling into the bottom 25% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth tests also place the instance in the bottom 25% for both small and large block read/write operations, though its PassMark memory score reaches the middle 50% average. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and small-model LLM inference prompt processing show poor performance in the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the r5dn.xlarge trades raw computational speed for high memory density and local NVMe SSD storage. This resource profile is suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high CPU throughput, such as caching layers, database operations with moderate transaction rates, and general-purpose memory-optimized tasks.
